scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in Southern California in 1978, with the Cuckoo's Nest in Costa Mesa often cited as its birthplace.
It evolved from the pogo dance of the 1970s British punk scene.
During the 1980s, it spread across the United States, with New York hardcore scenes blending the style with heavy metal influences.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Moshing is a form of crowd interaction at live music concerts.
While some participants view it as a positive form of fan expression, others criticize it for its violence and potential for injury.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: .unpalatable Punk Rock Disco 2 @ Unaffiliated 777 (vid,audio,info) (https://archive.org/details/unpalatable-unaffiliated-777)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance takes place in a 'pit' where participants push, slam, or collide.

Specific movements include the 'Huntington Beach Strut' (circling and swinging arms), 'two-stepping' (a running-in-place motion with crossed legs), and 'circle pits' (running in a circular motion around the edge of the pit).
Watch for Huntington Beach Strut, Two-step.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (xS5o0bZT4zY)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular or chaotic, within a designated 'pit'.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Moshing is typically performed to aggressive styles of music, including punk rock, hardcore, heavy metal, grunge, and occasionally hip-hop and electronic dance music.
The music is characterized by high energy, fast tempos, and often features rhythmic breakdowns.
Listen for the Electric guitar, Bass guitar, Drums, Vocals.
The pulse is 4/4.
Aggressive, high-tempo music with distorted guitars, driving drum beats, and intense vocal delivery.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: There is no specific costume for moshing; it is typically performed in casual concert attire.
The setting is a 'mosh pit,' a designated area of the crowd, often near the front of the stage or in the center of the venue floor.

scenes.title: The people
narration: H.R.
(Bad Brains), Sid Vicious (Sex Pistols), Scott Ian and Billy Milano (Stormtroopers of Death), and Mike Marine are frequently associated with the development or naming of the practice.

Variants include the 'Huntington Beach Strut,' 'Boston thrash' (punching below the neck), 'pig piles,' 'wrecking' (psychobilly scene), and the 'wall of death' (two sides of the crowd running at each other).
Descends from the British pogo; influenced the development of hardcore dancing and various sub-styles in metal and hip-hop.
